title: Serial Wire Debug (SWD) on a 2.54 mm single-row pin header, 4 or 5 pins
reference: skills/hw-design/references/interfaces.md §9 (rules H25-02 to H25-06) and §10 (H12-03 for the nRESET pull-up)
sources: No standard fixes the pin order of a 2.54 mm SWD header (interfaces.md §9.3). Roles match by symbol pin name; a generic Conn_01x0n symbol names its pins Pin_1..Pin_n, so state the order in PARTS[ref].pin_map.

VTref.description: target rail the probe senses its logic level from

rules.text: SWDIO, SWCLK, GND and VTref are each wired to another part.
The four required SWD pins are on four different nets.
The GND pin carries the board's ground net.
VTref is a rail, not ground.
When nRESET is brought out, it has a pull-up to the target rail, or the MCU's own pull-up is documented (H12-03: 10 to 100 kohm).
The header's pins are named on the silkscreen from the header's own side.
A header carrying a supply and a signal has a reversed-plug mitigation: GND on both ends, a shroud, or a documented risk.

notes: A vertical 2.54 mm header mates +z, a right-angle one +x (interfaces.md §9.2); declare it as PARTS[ref].mating_direction.
H25-01 (pitch, pin count, style) is kicad_fpcheck.py with a PinHeader-1x0<n>-2.54 PACKAGES entry, not this checker.
